title: Config
description: evals/litmustest.yaml. Where traces come from, how runs execute, how judges are trusted, what CI enforces, and where results go.

project.description: The project this evals/ folder belongs to.

format.description: otel and jsonl ship in Phase 1; the platform adapters are Phase 4.

path.description: A file or glob, relative to the repo root, for jsonl and otel. Ignored for platform formats.

project.description: For braintrust: the project id to pull logs from. Credentials come from the environment (BRAINTRUST_API_KEY; LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY, LANGFUSE_HOST).

sampler.description: How a review batch is drawn from the source.

clusters.description: Number of clusters; one representative per cluster, the rest random.

trials.description: Trials per task unless the task overrides.

concurrency.description: Trials running at the same time.

budget_usd.description: Stop starting new trials once the run's recorded cost (usage.cost_usd from each trial.json) reaches this. Trials already running finish; the run summary records what was skipped under `budget`. 0 or absent means no limit.

environment.description: Where each trial runs. inprocess: the command is a child process on this machine. docker: a fresh container per trial (see runs.docker). harbor: a one-trial Harbor job per trial (see runs.harbor).

cpus.description: CPU limit per trial. Applied by docker (--cpus) and harbor; not enforced in process.

memory_mb.description: Memory limit per trial in MB. Applied by docker (--memory) and harbor; not enforced in process.

timeout_s.description: Seconds before a trial is killed and tagged as an infra error (timeout). In process the whole process group is killed.

docker.description: For environment: docker. Each trial runs as `docker run --rm` with the trial directory mounted at /trial and evals/ mounted read-only at /evals; {trial_dir}, {task_file} and {evals} are filled with those container paths. The command goes to `sh -lc` inside the container. Give image or build.

image.description: An image that already exists locally or can be pulled.

build.description: Build the image once at the start of the run.

context.description: Build context, relative to the repo root.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path, relative to the repo root. Default: <context>/Dockerfile.

network.description: Passed to --network, e.g. none or host.

mounts.description: Extra volumes as host:container[:ro]. The host side is relative to the repo root.

workdir.description: Working directory inside the container (-w). Default: the image's own.

pass_env.description: Names of environment variables on this machine to pass into the container (an API key, for example). Only the name is written anywhere; the value is read from the environment at run time.

harbor.description: For environment: harbor (https://harborframework.com). Each trial is a generated Harbor task run once with Harbor's oracle agent, which runs the agent command inside the task's container. The trial directory is /logs/artifacts; the task file is at /solution/task.yaml; the rest of evals/ is not mounted, so bake what the command needs into the image.

image.description: The container image the command runs in (Harbor's [environment] docker_image).

backend.description: Harbor's environment backend, passed as `harbor run -e`. Default: Harbor's own default (docker).

pass_env.description: Names of environment variables on this machine to pass into the container (an API key, for example). Only the name is written anywhere; the value is read from the environment at run time.

default_model.description: Model used by a judge that does not pin its own. Must be a dated snapshot.

trust_threshold.description: TPR and TNR (percent) a judge needs on the held-out test set to be trusted.

stale_on_change.description: Mark a judge stale when its prompt hash or model changes.

correct_for_judge_error.description: Correct reported pass rates for the judge's measured TPR/TNR.

gates.description: Per-suite gates, keyed by suite name.

storage.description: Where run output goes. Summaries are small and go in git; transcripts are evidence and get a stable address.

backend.description: local: a git-ignored directory. s3 and gcs: one object per file. braintrust and langfuse: one trace per trial, tagged with run, task and trial. langsmith is not written yet and is refused with an error.

path.description: local: the directory, relative to the repo root (default .litmustest/transcripts). s3 and gcs: optionally the bucket URI (s3://bucket/prefix) instead of bucket and prefix.

bucket.description: s3 and gcs: the bucket name.

prefix.description: s3 and gcs: key prefix inside the bucket. Objects are <prefix>/<run id>/<task id>/<n>/<file>.

region.description: s3: the bucket's region. Default: AWS_REGION, then us-east-1.

endpoint.description: s3: a custom endpoint for an S3-compatible store (MinIO, R2); requests are then path-style.

project.description: braintrust: the project id to log to. Default: BRAINTRUST_PROJECT_ID.

transcripts.description: Where each trial's trial.json, grades.json, stdout.txt and stderr.txt go. The run summary names them by transcript_ref (local:, s3://, gs://, langfuse:, braintrust:). With a remote backend the runner works in a local cache under .litmustest/cache/ and uploads after grading; readers fetch what is missing and keep it there. Credentials come from the environment only: s3 reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and optionally AWS_SESSION_TOKEN and AWS_REGION; gcs reads GCS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and GCS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (HMAC keys for the S3-compatible XML API); langfuse reads LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_HOST; braintrust reads BRAINTRUST_API_KEY and BRAINTRUST_PROJECT_ID.

pr_comment.description: Post the comparison as a PR comment.

base_run.description: Which run a CI run is compared against.

agent.description: How the runner starts the agent for one trial. The command runs once per trial in a fresh trial directory and must leave <trial_dir>/trial.json in the reference_solution shape (output, state, tool_calls, transcript, optional usage and latency_ms). Placeholders: {task}, {task_file}, {trial_dir}, {trial}, {evals}; the same values arrive as LITMUSTEST_TASK, LITMUSTEST_TASK_FILE, LITMUSTEST_TRIAL_DIR, LITMUSTEST_TRIAL, LITMUSTEST_INPUT (JSON) and LITMUSTEST_EVALS. Under docker and harbor the paths are the ones inside the container and the command line goes to a shell there.

command.description: The command line, split on spaces (quotes respected), run without a shell.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to the repo root. Default: the repo root.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the agent.

reset.description: Optional command run before each trial to reset external state (a database, a sandbox). Same placeholders.

coverage.description: Maps of the application that `litmustest coverage` measures the eval suite against: spec (test-case ids in your docs), surface (API routes or tool names the trials actually call), risk (failure modes by severity, always on), traffic (the surface items production traces used, on when surface is set and traces are ingested), code (lines that ran during the suites, from a report your process writes) and frontend (pages the trials opened).

spec.description: Requirements: every match of id_pattern in these files is one item. A task covers an item through `covers:` or a `source: spec:<id>` (case-insensitive).

files.description: Paths or globs relative to the repository root.

id_pattern.description: A regular expression for one spec id, e.g. SYS-[A-Z]+-\\d+.

area_pattern.description: A regular expression with one capture group that picks the area from an id. Default: the id without its trailing number.

surface.description: What the product exposes. Items come from an OpenAPI file, a scan of route decorators, or an explicit list (tool names, for an agent). A route counts as exercised when a trial in the latest run calls it; `covers:` can also claim one.

openapi.description: Path to an OpenAPI JSON or YAML file, relative to the repository root.

scan.description: Globs of source files to scan for route decorators such as @app.get("/path") or router.post('/path').

items.description: An explicit list: "METHOD /path" or tool names.

ignore.description: Items to leave out, matched exactly or by a trailing *.

group_depth.description: How many path segments make an area for the chart. Default 2 (/api/play).

code.description: Code that ran while the suites ran. litmustest instruments nothing: your agent's own process has to write the report (for example with c8, nyc or coverage.py's lcov output) during `litmustest run`.

report.description: Path to an lcov tracefile or an Istanbul JSON report (coverage-final.json or coverage-summary.json), relative to the repository root.

ignore.description: Files to leave out. A trailing * matches a prefix.

group_depth.description: How many leading path segments make an area. Default 1.

frontend.description: The product's pages. A page counts as exercised when a trial in the latest run opened its URL (a tool call whose url or path matches); `covers:` can also claim one.

scan.description: Globs of source files to scan: Next.js app/ and pages/ folders by file name, React Router and Vue Router files by their path declarations.

ignore.description: Routes to leave out. A trailing * matches a prefix.

learn_more_url.description: Base URL of the Master Class guide. Learn more links go to <url>#ch-<n>; without it the chapter is named but not linked.

plain_language_default.description: Whether Plain language starts on for someone who has not chosen. Each person's own choice lives in ~/.config/litmustest/prefs.json, not here.
